who: Christian Rudolf Raschle, historian of Rome and late antiquity at Université de Montréal, doctorate Fribourg.

evidence.says: History faculty profile lists Roman history and late antiquity, and Raphaël Weyland’s 2020 doctorate on Seleucia among his supervised theses.
The history faculty roster names Christian Rudolf Raschle, associate professor, with a doctorate from Fribourg, Switzerland.
Authority identifies Christian Rudolf Raschle, author of Pestes Harenae; its source note records a 1999 doctorate in Latin philology and teaching at Basel and Fribourg.

notes: The university supplies the full name distinguishing the selected candidate from the separate Christian Raschle authority n85350914.

who: Jüri Kivimäe, historian of the Baltic region and Toronto’s Chair of Estonian Studies, 1999–2017.

evidence.says: Toronto’s profile of history PhD alumnus Joseph Sproule explicitly names Jüri Kivimäe as his supervisor and describes his research on Baltic mercenaries.
The retirement notice records Kivimäe’s appointment in 1999 and retirement in 2017; it identifies Joseph Sproule as his sixth-year PhD student.
Authority for Kivimäe, Jüri cites Tartu university personnel records, an Estonian Academy of Sciences history, and his Baltic historical publications.

notes: Direct student-supervisor evidence confirms the name and institution. The doctorate institution in own_phd was not independently verified.

who: Denis Smyth, University of Toronto historian of modern international relations, PhD history Cambridge 1978.

evidence.says: Trinity’s profile gives a Cambridge history PhD in 1978, research on diplomacy and strategy, and publications on Franco’s Spain and wartime intelligence.
The licensed publisher preview of Revolution and War in Spain identifies Denis Smyth as professor of modern history at Toronto and coauthor of Spain, the EEC and NATO (1984).
Authority identifies Denis Smyth through Paul Preston and Denis Smyth’s Spain, the EEC, and NATO (1984).

notes: The shared book connects the LC candidate to Toronto; Cambridge matches own_phd. The other Denis Smyth authority, n93025847, identifies the author of Poet of the People.

who: Aldona Sendzikas, Western University historian of twentieth-century and military history, PhD Hawaiʻi.

evidence.says: Western lists Aldona Sendzikas as supervisor of Allen Priest’s 2021 dissertation In the Shadow of the Atomic Cloud.
The faculty roster lists Aldona Sendzikas as associate professor of history with a PhD from Hawaii.
The department lists her Lucky 73: USS Pampanito’s Unlikely Rescue of Allied POWs in WWII (2010).
Authority identifies Aldona Sendzikas through USS Pampanito’s Unlikely Rescue of Allied POWs in WWII (2010).

notes: Exact supervised dissertation, matching doctorate institution, and shared publication establish the match.

who: William Milligan Sloane, Columbia historian and head of its history department, 1896–1916.

evidence.says: Columbia identifies William Milligan Sloane as Seth Low Professor and department head from 1896 to 1916, encompassing both students’ doctorate years.
Authority identifies William Milligan Sloane and cites his historical work The Balkans.
The alternative William Sloane authority identifies a publisher and science-fiction author whose works include To Walk the Night.

notes: The full name, discipline and Columbia career identify n86821156; nr95031854 describes a different writer.

who: George Urdang, University of Wisconsin–Madison professor and historian of pharmacy, founding director of AIHP.

evidence.says: ASHP records that Glenn Sonnedecker studied under George Urdang at Wisconsin–Madison and received his history of pharmacy and science PhD in 1952.
Wisconsin identifies Urdang as a pharmacy professor, founder of the graduate program, and collaborator on Kremers and Urdang’s History of Pharmacy.
Authority for George Urdang records the variant Georg Urdang and cites Kremers and Urdang’s History of Pharmacy.

notes: The named student, 1952 degree, institution and shared textbook confirm the candidate.

who: Jane Boulden, Royal Military College professor of international relations and UN security studies, PhD political studies Queen’s 1998.

evidence.says: Queen’s identifies Jane Boulden as an RMC professor and Canada Research Chair there from 2004 to 2014; her fields include UN sanctions and peacekeeping, and it lists a 2010 publication with Andrea Charron.
The thesis title page identifies Jane Boulden’s Chapter Seven and a Quarter: The United Nations and the Dilemmas of Mandate Enforcement as a Queen’s political studies PhD thesis, October 1998.
Authority identifies Jane Boulden through the same 1998 Queen’s political studies doctoral thesis.

notes: The exact dissertation connects the LC identity to the academic; her RMC appointment covers 2010 and her UN research agrees with the students’ subjects.

who: F. Russell Bryant, historian of modern Britain at the University of Alabama.

evidence.says: Alabama’s history department recalls F. Russell Bryant teaching modern British history for thirty years, including the undergraduate years of a 1981 graduate.
The National Library of Wales newsletter identifies the editor of The Coalition Diaries and Letters of H. A. L. Fisher, 1916–1922 as Dr F. Russell Bryant, formerly of the University of Alabama.
Authority identifies F. Russell Bryant through The Coalition Diaries and Letters of H. A. L. Fisher, 1916–1922 (2006).

notes: The shared Fisher edition explicitly connects the LC candidate to Alabama; the department confirms his field and presence during the students’ period.
